From the owner
How the material process actually works: You pick the tile. The cabinets. The counters. The faucets, the lighting, the colors. That part is where a remodel gets heavy. If you are doing it yourself, you are the one calling the store, the cabinet guy, the counter place, and the plumber, and none of them have the same picture of the job. You get a stack of links and a deadline. You guess. Something shows up that does not fit the room, or it blows the number, and you find out in week three. That is not how I work. After we sign, the vendor already has the job before the appointment is even made. The layout, the sizes, and the allowance. You are not walking in cold. You walk in, point at what you like, and walk out. I am there for the color and the style, and we hold every pick up against the allowance before anything gets ordered. If it blows the number, you hear it there, not after it shows up. That help is part of the job. Not a charge. You are not managing vendors. You are not chasing lead times. You are not wondering what got left out. You pick. I order it. I install it. I run the whole job. I ran manufacturing for years before this. The job was already planned before anyone touched it. I still work that way. That is what makes start to finish actually finish.
Oct 6, 2026

From the owner
Phillips Property Solutions, LLC transformed a dated bathroom and laundry area in Memphis, TN with 3D rendering, thoughtful space planning, and coordinated finishes. Our bathroom remodeling and 3D design services helped the homeowner visualize a better layout before demolition. Relocating the toilet created room for a custom walk-in shower, improved traffic flow, and added practical storage. The renovation included removal of the prefabricated shower and existing vanity, plumbing modifications, and construction of a new shower knee wall. Large-format white and gray shower wall tile paired with complementary mosaic tile on the shower floor and niche created a clean, modern look. A glass shower enclosure and door allowed light to flow through the space. A new 24-inch vanity, vanity mirror, and brushed nickel fixtures and hardware completed the bathroom. Custom Timber Toffee wall cabinets above the washer and dryer added convenient laundry storage. Agreeable Gray walls and pure white trim and door finishes brought the room together. From 3D project visualization and demolition to plumbing, tile installation, and finishing details, our team delivered a more functional bathroom and laundry room.
